title: Ice Cream Cone, Soft Serve, Chocolate

content.title: About
content.content: Soft‑serve chocolate ice cream in a crunchy waffle cone is a classic treat featuring creamy ice cream coated with a thin chocolate glaze and served in a crisp cone. Portion size: 450 ml.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ice‑cream cone was introduced in the United States in the early 1900s.
Chocolate glaze often contains cocoa butter, which gives it a glossy, snap‑crisp finish.
Soft‑serve is typically served at about –6 °C, making it lighter and airier than regular ice cream.
In some countries the cones are decorated with nuts, sprinkles, or caramel drizzle.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium essential for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk and cream used in the recipe are rich in vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from cocoa
items.content: Chocolate glaze contains flavonoids that may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large servings can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains dairy, which may cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Allergy to nuts or soy emulsifiers
items.content: Chocolate glaze may contain nuts or soy lecithin, potential allergens for some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve immediately after preparation to keep the cone crunchy and the ice cream soft. Optionally garnish with sprinkles, fresh berries, or an extra drizzle of chocolate sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a freezer at –18 °C for no more than 2 weeks. Avoid repeated thawing to preserve the texture of the soft‑serve.
